region: Gevrey-Chambertin · Côte de Nuits, Burgundy, France
about: Domaine Trapet-Rochelandet is a small family estate in the heart of Gevrey-Chambertin, on the Rue du Chambertin, across from the village’s Rôtisserie du Chambertin. It is a lesser-known branch of the Trapet name: the former Domaine François Trapet, which Laurent Rochelandet took on as his father retired, renaming it in 2015 to honour the vines his mother brought to the family. Laurent studied at the wine school in Beaune and made his first vintage in 2008. Since 2013 he has bottled far more of his own harvest instead of selling grapes to négociants.

The estate covers about six and a half hectares, from village Gevrey-Chambertin through the Premiers Crus Petite Chapelle and Bel Air to a parcel of Grand Cru Ruchottes-Chambertin. Bel Air lies at the very top of the Gevrey slope, just below the forest, on limestone-rich soils. Its grapes ripen later than those lower down, which gives the wine a cooler, more mineral style. Laurent avoids new oak, working with used barrels largely from his neighbour Domaine Philippe Leclerc, and has cut yields in recent years for greater intensity and focus.

Writers who follow the domaine describe Bel Air as its most mineral wine: elegant and cool, with an “airy” tone and plenty of red forest berries, and noticeably more mineral than the Petite Chapelle. The 2021 vintage in Burgundy was a cool, low-yielding year, a style that tends to suit a high, late-ripening site like this one.
facts: Premier Cru Bel Air, top of the Gevrey-Chambertin slope just below the forest
About 6.5 ha, family-run by Laurent Rochelandet
